html:
Carthage was founded on the coast of today's Tunisia by settlers from the Phoenician city of Tyre, by tradition in 814 BCE. Legend names its founder as the princess Dido.

Its harbour faced the narrows between Africa and Sicily, and it grew into the leading city of the Phoenician west. By the 400s BCE Carthage ruled an empire of trading posts and farmland from Libya to Spain, with a great navy and a council of rich families.

Its wars with Rome over Sicily and Spain, the Punic Wars, ended with the city's destruction in 146 BCE (Rome destroys Carthage). Rome rebuilt it as the capital of its province of Africa. Its general Hannibal remains Tunisia's most famous ancient name.
